title: GROWING INDIA-VIETNAM DEFENCE RELATIONS
author: Codings
text:
**_Growing defence ties between New Delhi and Hanoi in the last few years are fostering tensions in Beijing as China and Vietnam have crossed swords over the South China Sea and India has been recently vocal about Vietnam's stance on the application of international law and the peaceful settlement of conflicts in the South China Sea. This increasing partnership between India and Vietnam can act as a counterbalance to the rising influence of China in the region and might compel Beijing to retrospect its current stance of the South China Sea._**

In recent years, relations between India and Vietnam have reached a greater height, especially in the defence sector. The strength of the commitment towards stronger ties can be seen by the fact that India, in a first, transferred an indigenously built in-service missile corvette, INS Kirpan, of the Indian Navy to Vietnam People’s Navy [in June 2023](https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1936047) and handed over to Vietnam People’s Navy on July 22nd, 2023 by Indian Chief of Naval Staff Admiral R Hari Kumar [at Cam Ranh in Vietnam](https://indianexpress.com/article/india/in-latest-move-towards-growing-ties-india-hands-over-missile-corvette-ins-kirpan-to-vietnam-8856051/). The announcement was made by the Indian Defence Minister Rajanth Singh during a visit of the Vietnamese counterpart Gen Phan Van Giang to India from 17-19 June. This transfer has been seen as the fulfilment of [India’s commitment](https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1936047) to assist ‘like-minded partners’ to enhance their defensive capabilities. The handover of the INS Kirpan to Vietnam serves as one of the many steps taken by India to fulfil the objectives of the ambitious SAGAR (Security and Growth for All in the Region) initiative and also the principles of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.These growing defence ties between New Delhi and Hanoi are fostering tensions in Beijing as China and Vietnam have crossed swords over the South China Sea and India has been recently vocal about Vietnam's stance on the application of international law and the peaceful settlement of conflicts in the South China Sea.

**Birth of India-Vietnam Defence Ties**

India had made ties with and has also been involved in Vietnam since its independence, as can be witnessed with Indian PM Pandit Nehru’s visit to Vietnam in 1954 and India [being the chairman](https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Vietnam_new2021.pdf) of the International Commission for Supervision and Control (ICSC) to aid the peace process in Vietnam. With the launch of the Look East Policy by India in 1994 under Narasimha Rao, India and Vietnam [signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)](https://orfonline.org/wp-content/uploads/2013/11/IssueBrief_60.pdf) on Defence Cooperation Agreement centred on military exchanges, visits, and training. When Vietnamese PM Phan Van Khai visited India in 2000, the two countries inked one of their early defence cooperation agreements, which paved the way for further cooperation between the two forces. The focus of India-Vietnam defence cooperation and a significant element of the bilateral strategic relations has been training, joint exercises, exchange of protocols, and operational manuals. India and Vietnam have also developed naval cooperation, which includes joint training programmes for aviation, dockyards, and submarines. In 2014, during Indian President Pranab Mukherjee’s visit, India announced a US [$100 million line of credit](https://www.mea.gov.in/Portal/ForeignRelation/Vi_Bilateral_Relations_December_2018__1_.pdf) to Vietnam. As a part of it, a contract of 12 offshore patrol vessels was signed between the Vietnam Border Guards and M/s. Larsen & Toubro Ltd. in September 2016. PM Modi [announced a new line of credit](https://thewire.in/external-affairs/india-and-vietnam-upgrade-to-comprehensive-strategic-partnership) worth US $500 million during his visit to Vietnam in 2016, as well as US $5 million in funding for the construction of an Army Software Park at the Telecommunications University in Nha Trang. In India’s Act East Policy, which focusses on extended neighbourhood in the Asia-Pacific region, Vietnam is an important pillar and the very fact is admitted by the Indian PM Narendra Modi [during virtual summit](https://www.outlookindia.com/website/story/india-news-vietnam-an-important-pillar-of-indias-act-east-policy-prime-minister-narendra-modi/367935) with Vietnamese Prime Minister Nguyen Xuan Phuc in 2020. Vietnam is important for India as it not only an important trading partner or a defence partner in the region but also it supports India’s claim for [the permanent seat in the UNSC.](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/politics-and-nation/vietnam-reaffirms-support-for-indias-permanent-membership-in-unsc-mea/videoshow/79845046.cms)

Both countries have also been conducting Security Dialogues since November 2003. the [13th edition took place](https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1687915) in January 2021 and for the first time, labelled as ‘Defence Security Dialogue’. Marine cooperation is an important aspect of the bilateral relationship and the inaugural India-Vietnam Marine Security Dialogue was conducted in March 2019. India is increasing its participation in the Vietnamese defence sector by enhancing current services to [upgrade the current stock of Soviet-era military hardware](https://www.export.gov/apex/article2?id=Vietnam-Defense-Sector), including thermal sights fire control systems for armoured vehicles, T-54 and T-55 tanks, and M-17/MI-8 helicopters, as well as upgrading Vietnam's Petya-class light frigates for anti-submarine warfare. This is so because India itself has been a long term Russian defence partner and seasoned of the Russian military technology. Vietnam's reliance on Russia is reduced by India's ability to train its military personnel on Russia's Su-30 Fighter and Kilo Class submarines. India is rising as the defence exporter at the global stage and Vietnam could benefit from it in the long term as the Indian military hardware is lot cheaper than compared to US and that of other European countries. India also offers line of credit. Brahmos cruise missiles, the Akash missile air defence system, Varunastra anti-submarine torpedoes, and coastal radars have all [been offered by India to Vietnam](https://www.orfonline.org/expert-speak/the-importance-of-indias-defence-partnership-with-vietnam/). Since sanctions have been imposed on Moscow by the West amid the Russian-Ukraine conflict, the need arises for Vietnam to look for different defence partners and be more self-reliant. And the ‘Joint Vision Statement on the India-Vietnam Defence Partnership towards 2030’ signed by the two defence ministers in June 2022, which aims to enhance the scope and scale of existing defence cooperation, could be step towards that.

**Why It Concerns China?**

It is not a hidden fact that China has differences with both India and Vietnam on border issues. Since the Galwan incident in 2020, tensions are present in the LAC even after a series of talks between the officials of both sides. On the other hand, Vietnam has settled its territorial border disputes with China after completing a decade-long [demarcation of the border in 2009](http://www.china.org.cn/world/2009-11/19/content_18915108.htm#:~:text=China%20and%20Vietnam%20signed%20land%20boundary%20treaty%20in,land%20border%20with%20about%202%2C000%20border%20markers%20erected.). Even though the dispute over the land border has been resolved between Vietnam and China, the major dispute between the two still lies in the South China Sea, where there is an undefined maritime border and disputes over the territorial waters and the ownership of islands like the Spratly and Paracel Islands are present. Both China and Vietnam have accused each other’s boats of violating their exclusive economic zone (EEZ), and instances of confrontation have also come between the two sides for a long time, whether it be the confrontation between the two in 2014, in which the matter escalated to the [ramming of ships](https://www.nytimes.com/2014/05/08/world/asia/philippines-detains-crew-of-chinese-fishing-vessel.html), or recently in May 2023 when [Chinese vessels ignored](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/chinese-ships-ignore-vietnam-demand-leave-area-close-russian-run-gas-fields-2023-05-26/) Vietnam’s demand to leave its EEZ.

In a dispute involving China's maritime claims, a UNCLOS-established international arbitral tribunal decided in favour of the Philippines in 2016 and declared the nine-dash line to be without legal foundation. However, the decision was rejected by China as it claims its own ‘nine-dash line’ as the demarcation of the maritime border in the South China Sea, and if China agrees to UNCLOS, it would have a great negative impact on the strategic advantage of China in the region. The South China Sea is important for the region as it is the second most used waterway in the world with trade worth US $200 billion passing through every year. [According to an estimate](https://chinapower.csis.org/much-trade-transits-south-china-sea/) approximately 40 percent of the China’s total trade and 80 percent of energy imports passed through the South China Sea in 2016. The Sea is an important fishing ground for the Southeast Asian nations. The stability and peace in the South China Sea are essential for Vietnam as 80 percent of its people reside within 160 km of the coast of the Sea. This sea also facilitates 86 percent of Hanoi’s trade with the outside world and have many oil fields. India’s ONGC Videsh has been active with Vietnam in the oil exploration and drilling in the sea. India has been asked to help Vietnam and other ASEAN countries stabilise naval cooperation and counterbalance China’s aggression in the area.

It is well known that India is interested in the Indo-Pacific and sees the area as an organic maritime space with the ASEAN at its centre. India and Vietnam signed an agreement in October 2011 for the promotion and expansion of oil exploration in the South China Sea which is objected to by China. A strong India and Vietnam are in no interest of China and with increasing defence ties between Hanoi and New Delhi, the long-term objectives of Beijing in the region could be threatened as India poses a direct competition to the Chinese hegemony in the region and Beijing is aware of this. In 2011, the official Chinese news agency Xinhua [stated that](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/china-harasses-indian-naval-ship-on-south-china-sea/articleshow/9829900.cms) increasing India-Vietnam relations would create challenges for China and in 2016 [The Global Times warned India](https://idsa.in/idsacomments/why-india-south-china-sea-stand-matters_asingh_190816) that India posture towards South China Sea would harm the relations between the two. n April 2023, during a delegation-level meeting on bilateral security cooperation between India and Vietnam, [one of the major dimensions](https://en.bocongan.gov.vn/international-relations-cooperation/vietnam-india-agree-to-expand-security-cooperation-t9909.html) of the meeting was both parties reaffirmed their commitment to preserving and advancing peace, stability, marine safety, and freedom of overflight and navigation in the Indo-Pacific region. Not mentioning the name of China, its aggressive policies in the South China Sea and Indo-Tibetan border were discussed and both parties underlined their stance that any conflicts must be settled peacefully while upholding international law without the use of threats, violence, or a unilateral or coercive change in the status quo. Both India and Vietnam are increasing their defence expenditure and trying to build a force of deterrence. [According to the Stockholm](https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/vietnam-defense-and-security-sector) International Peace Research Institute, some of the highest increases in military spending in Southeast Asia have been in Vietnam. From USD 841 million in 2003 to USD 5.5 billion in 2018, its military budget surged by over 700 per cent between 2003 and 2018. For the first time, Vietnam hosted an international defence expo in 2022 seeking to diversify its defence procurement. A strong Vietnam is in no interest of China as it could possess a threat to China’s long-term strategic interests in the South China Sea.

**Conclusion**

Vietnam has become an important pillar for India’s Act East Policy and Indo-Pacific Vision in Southeast Asia. Both countries are advancing in their strategic partnership and planning to go past the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership; defence and security cooperation is an important element of this partnership. In the areas of the Blue Economy and maritime security, India and Vietnam may mutually gain from one another. Both India and Vietnam view their partnerships strategically for the long term and are certain that working together will assist to maintain peace and stability in the region.

This increasing partnership between India and Vietnam can act as a counterbalance to the rising influence of China in the region and might compel Beijing to retrospect its current stance on the South China Sea dispute. As a result of their strategic alliance, India and Vietnam are now able to negotiate changing regional dynamics and address prevalent issues such as those brought on by China's rise. Their cooperation strengthens Indo-Pacific peace and security and fosters the development of a more balanced regional structure, as this cooperation acts against the birth of hegemony by any power in the region and rather promotes multipolarity.

title: Dhami govt offers sops to Agniveers, toughens Anti-Conversion law
author: Uniindia News Service
text: States » North Posted at: Aug 14 2025 12:44AM Dehradun, Aug 13 (UNI) In an important move, the Uttarakhand government has decided to reserve its 10 percent jobs for Agniveer defence personnel in the state. The Dhami government has also decided to increase punishment under the anti-religious conversion law from 10 to maximum 20 years or even life imprisonment and fine amount from ₹50,000 to one lakh. The Pushkar Singh Dhami cabinet on Wednesday decided to give 10 percent horizontal reservation for Agniveers in contractual positions in government jobs. The decision came at the time when the first batch of Agniveer defence personnel will soon complete its service tenure and return to their homes. This coincides with the Dhami government's plan to fill 850 posts in various departments by Agniveers on contract. Pposts identified for accommodating Agniveers are in Group C category including constables and sub inspectors ​in fire and civil police, Jail Police, Forest Guard, patwari in revenue department, excise and state transport departments.

title: Realme P1 Speed launched in India with great specifications  check here
author: Abhijeet V Singh
text:
- [Home](https://content.techgig.com/)
- [Technology](https://content.techgig.com/technology)
- Realme P1 Speed launched in India with great specifications; check here

# Realme P1 Speed launched in India with great specifications; check here

741 Views \| 16 Oct 2024, 07:48 PM \| Updated on: 16 Oct 2024, 07:48 PM \|
Abhijeet V Singh

Realme has launched the third variation in the P1 series titled ‘Speed.’ This year’s launch packs a punch way above its weight with a performance-to-price ratio. Here’s an overview.

[Realme](https://content.techgig.com/searchresult.cms?query=realme) launched the P1 series earlier this year, completely disrupting the market. The phone came with fantastic design, performance, hardware, and pricing. This time, the company has launched the P1 Speed model with many impressive features. **Design and Display of [Realme P1 Speed](https://content.techgig.com/searchresult.cms?query=realme+p1+speed)** The P1 Speed shares a stylish design with its siblings. Once again, breaking the norms brings you an [OLED screen](https://content.techgig.com/searchresult.cms?query=oled+screen) with a [120Hz refresh rate](https://content.techgig.com/searchresult.cms?query=120hz+refresh+rate). Its 6'67 inch flat display offers a peak brightness of 2,000 nits. This easily matches various flagship models. The front also comes with a 16 MP punch-hole camera.The design is identical to the previous P1 models, with no notable differences. There are two colour schemes: textured titanium and brushed blue. **Performance of P1 Speed** The P1 Speed is powered by the [MediaTek Dimensity 7300](https://content.techgig.com/searchresult.cms?query=mediatek+dimensity+7300) Energy processor under the hood. It offers two variations with 8GB and 12 GB of RAM. There is also a 128 and 256 GB storage variation. However, these are UFS 3.1 storage. Thus bringing best-in-class speed and performance.For additional benefits, you could use the dynamic RAM feature. It enables you to use the storage space for up to 14 GB of RAM. Making it more of a monster in performance. **A budget gaming beast** Designed with gamers in mind, the P1 Speed features a display certified for lag-free performance. It easily maintains 90 FPS even when the battery is running low. It includes a stainless steel vapour chamber for efficient cooling and Realme's GT Mode for enhanced gaming optimisation.This easily offers a highly competitive smartphone with gaming performance in mind. It might easily match heavy hitters in the performance segments. **The standard camera and battery** The phone's rear has a 50MP primary camera and a 2MP portrait camera. While Realme's models are usually hit or miss with the camera, this specification does the job. The specifications are still worth the consideration.It houses a robust [5000mAh battery](https://content.techgig.com/searchresult.cms?query=5000mah+battery) that supports [45W fast charging](https://content.techgig.com/searchresult.cms?query=45w+fast+charging) (charger included). This can be a bit downer as 6,000mAh and above has become the norm for performance phones. 67+ watts of charging is also a norm. However, given the low impact on the performance ratio, it is still a great configuration. **A fantastic array of extra features** Other notable features of [Realme P1](https://content.techgig.com/searchresult.cms?query=realme+p1) Speed include stereo speakers, dual SIM support, Wi-Fi 6, and Bluetooth 5.4. More importantly, it comes with a 3.5 mm jack option. You can have flawless connectivity and the best sound output with the device.Moreover, it matches the premium features with an IP65 dust and water resistance rating. # These buyers of physical shares are at legal and financial risk if they don't do this within a six-month window

By

[Neelanjit Das](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/etreporter/author-neelanjit-das-479259731.cms)

, ET OnlineLast Updated: Jul 23, 2025, 11:14:58 AM IST

[Follow us](https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va54SU83rZZYg2XcdM0K)

Share

Font Size

AbcSmall

AbcMedium

AbcLarge

Save

[Print](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/wealth/invest/these-buyers-of-physical-shares-are-at-legal-and-financial-risk-if-they-dont-do-this-within-a-six-month-window/printarticle/122638429.cms)

Comment

### Synopsis

Physical Shares Transfer: SEBI has provided a six-month window, from July 7, 2025, to January 6, 2026, for equity shareholders to re-lodge their physical share transfer deeds. This opportunity addresses deeds lodged before April 1, 2019, but were rejected due to deficiencies. Failure to re-lodge by the deadline puts buyers at legal and financial risk, potentially losing their shareholding rights. Read to know more.

ET OnlineHow claiming indexation benefit can help you pay lower capital gains tax on real estate sale transactions

In a bid to safeguard the interest of equity share buyers, the Securities And Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has recently notified that equity shareholders who missed the original deadline of March 21, 2021 to re-lodge their share transfer deed for [physical shares](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/physical-shares) can now do so, via a special six-month long window starting from July 7, 2025 to January 6, 2026.

Income Tax Guide

[Income Tax Slabs FY 2025-26](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/wealth/income-tax-slabs) [Income Tax Calculator 2025](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/wealth/calculators/income-tax-calculator) [New Income Tax Bill 2025](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/wealth/new-income-tax-bill-2025)

If this share transfer deed isn’t re-lodged, buyers of these equity [shares](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/shares) risk losing their their rights to them. This could lead to a situation where buyers have paid the sellers for these shares, but the company’s records don’t recognise them as shareholders. Consequently, once the special six-month window closes, one might end up with unverified physical share certificates, that can’t be sold, transferred, or converted into demat. That’s why you should act now.

## What did SEBI say?

SEBI in a notification dated July 2, 2025 said:

- Transfer of securities in physical mode was discontinued with effect from April 01,2019. Subsequently, it was clarified that transfer deeds lodged prior to deadline of April 01, 2019 and rejected/returned due to deficiency in the documents may be re-lodged with requisite documents. It was further decided to fix March 31, 2021 as the cut-off date for re-lodgement of transfer deeds.
- SEBI received representation from investors as well as RTAs and listed companies that some of the investors had missed the timelines for re-lodging their documents for transfer of securities.
- Thus, in order to facilitate ease of investing for investors and to secure the rights of investors in the securities which were purchased by them, it has been decided to open a special window only for re-lodgement of transfer deeds -- which were lodged before the April 01, 2019 deadline and rejected/returned/not attended to due to deficiency in the documents/process/or otherwise -- for a period of six months from July 07, 2025 till January 06, 2026.
- During this period, the securities that are re-lodged for transfer (including those requests that are pending with the listed company / RTA, as on date) shall be issued only in the demat mode. Due process shall be followed for such transfer-cum-demat requests.

## What does this SEBI notification mean?

Rohit Jain, Managing Partner, Singhania & Co. explains: “As per SEBI’s 2019 circular and subsequent clarifications including the present notification, Investors can continue to hold shares in physical form.However, transfer of securities (except transmission or transposition) cannot be processed unless the shares are held in a dematerialised form. So, while holding physical shares is not illegal, selling or transferring them is not allowed unless the shares are converted into demat form.”Also read: [NRIs to pay lower LTCG tax on these equity shares due to proposed forex fluctuation benefit in New Income Tax Bill 2025](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/wealth/tax/nris-to-pay-lower-ltcg-tax-on-these-equity-shares-due-to-proposed-forex-fluctuation-benefit-in-new-income-tax-bill-2025/articleshow/121466394.cms)

## Which [stock market](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/markets/stocks) investors are eligible for this six month long special re-lodgement window?

According to Anita Jain, an investment funds, asset management and regulatory lawyer, this six-month-long special window applies specifically to cases where such requests were originally submitted before April 01, 2019, but were rejected, returned, or left unprocessed due to documentation errors or procedural lapses.Jain adds: “This one-time relief is intended for investors who were unable to meet the earlier re-lodgement deadline of March 31, 2021. All transfer requests re-lodged during this window will be processed only in a dematerialised (demat) form.”

## If physical transfer deeds are not re-lodged by January 6, 2026, are the buyers' shareholding rights at risk?

Armin Pardiwala, Partner at HSA Advocates, says: “Yes, if the physical transfer deeds are not re-lodged by January 6, 2026, then buyers are at legal and financial risk.” Pardiwala explains why buyers could lose their shareholding rights if they don’t take advantage of this special six-month window to re-lodge the physical share transfer deeds. “If a buyer has acquired physical securities prior to April 1, 2019, but the transfer deed was rejected or returned due to documentation deficiencies, and the buyer fails to re-lodge the corrected transfer request by January 6, 2026, then:

- The legal title to the securities would remain with the original holder (i.e. the seller) and,
- The buyer, despite having paid for the securities, will not be recognized as the shareholder by the company.”

Pardiwala says: “Therefore, the buyer is at risk, as the legal title to the securities has not yet been transferred to them until the company registers the buyer’s name in its records. This is also re-affirmed in SEBI’s circular dated July 2, 2025, which states that the six-month window to re-lodge the transfer deeds is “in order to facilitate ease of investing for investors and to secure the rights of investors in the securities which were purchased by them”. Pranav Bhaskar, Senior Partner and Head of Corporate Practice, SKV Law Offices, agrees with Pardiwala and adds:” In the event, the buyers who paid for shares but couldn’t complete the transfer due to document issues, failure to utilise this special six-month-long window could risk leaving the buyers with no legal title and right to the securities purchased by them. In the event the buyers miss the extended deadline as well, such buyers may have to avail legal remedies before civil courts in a complex, costly process awaiting an uncertain outcome.”Sanchit Vijay, Founder, The Wealth Finder, agrees with Bhaskar and Pardiwala and adds: “Failure to re-lodge the transfer deeds, could mean the shares remain legally registered in the seller’s name, and the buyer — despite having paid — would lose legal ownership and rights over the shares. They wouldn’t be able to sell, vote, or claim dividends, and legal recovery would be difficult.”

## Buyers or sellers who are needed to re-lodge their physical transfer deeds?

Pardiwala from HSA Advocates, says that as per Section 56 of the Companies Act, 2013, permits either the seller (i.e. the transferor) or the buyer (i.e. the transferee) to lodge the instrument of transfer to the company for registering the transfer of securities. Pallavi Puri, Partner, DMD Advocates, says that prior to April 1, 2019, buyers could buy shares via physical transfer deed (SH-4 form), signed by both buyer and seller and submitted to the company’s RTA (Registrar and Transfer Agent). Puri adds: “However, post April 1, 2019, physical share transfers were discontinued and all such physical transfer deeds that were executed before April 1, 2019 had to be lodged with the company by March 31, 2021. So buyers had to submit the share transfer deed (duly signed by the seller) and physical certificates with the company/ RTA to protect their title/ownership to the shares. Once lodged, the company would register the buyer as the owner of the shares in physical form.”Jain adds that this six-month-long special window provides relief specifically for investors who have physical share certificates with valid transfer deeds. These investors had failed to have the shares transferred to their names due to technical issues such as mismatched signatures of the transferor against the company’s records, incorrect stamp duty, incomplete documentation, or improperly filled forms.Abhimanyu Bhattacharya, Partner at Khaitan & Co, explains:

- In order to facilitate ease of investing for investors and to protect the rights of investors in the securities which were purchased by them (buyers), SEBI has decided to open a special window from July 7, 2025 – January 6, 2026 only for purposes re-lodgement of transfer deeds, which were lodged prior to the deadline of April 1, 2019 and rejected/returned due to deficiency in documents or process.
- During this period, the securities that are re-lodged for transfer shall be issued by listed companies only in demat form. Since, transfer of physical shares is no longer possible, it would be prudent for all shareholders who hold shares in physical form to complete the demat process as soon as possible.

## Is this your last chance to secure your shareholding ownership digitally?

Puri explains that while there is no deadline (yet) to demat shares just for holding, i.e., you can legally hold them in physical form indefinitely, “but if the buyer:

- Acquired shares via a physical transfer deed, but never got them transferred his/her name (i.e., lodged the requisite documents with the company/ RTA), the window is only open till January 6, 2026.
- Also, if the buyer wants to sell or transfer shares in future, demat is mandatory.”

Puri says: “So while it’s not illegal to hold shares physically, doing so is becoming increasingly risky and outdated. SEBI’s direction is clear: digitisation of securities is the future. A demat is required for unlisted public companies and private transactions also now.”Bhaskar from SKV Law Offices, says: Investors can convert their shares to demat form at any time and are not subject to the deadline mentioned in the present [SEBI Circular](https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/topic/sebi-circular).Bhaskar adds: “An investor who has physical certificates with clear and undisputed ownership of the securities may face no immediate deadline pressure and can dematerialise their holdings at any time through their depository participant. The Extended Deadline concerns the incomplete transfer transactions, and not the routine dematerialisation of physical shares held by the investors with an undisputed title and right.”Jain from Singhania & Co. explains:

- If you already own shares in your name (i.e., not acquired through a transfer), you can dematerialise them anytime. But if you have physical shares that you bought from someone else, and the transfer was never completed, then January 6, 2026, is likely your final opportunity to regularize the ownership.
- So, for transferees with pending transfer deeds, this is indeed your last legal window to get the shares transferred into your name, and then dematerialise them. Once this window closes, you may be stuck with unverified physical certificates, which cannot be sold, transferred, or converted into demat form.

Pardiwala says: The broker’s statement may be practically correct. From a practical standpoint, if the transfer of shares in physical form is restricted, then holding them does not serve any tangible purpose, since the investor may not be able to sell or monetise them when needed. Having said that, legally speaking, there is no restriction on holding securities in physical form. Also, there is no deadline for dematerialisation of securities held in physical form. An investor can get their securities dematerialised anytime and upon dematerialisation, are allowed to transfer the securities.

## What does Section 56(1) of the Companies Act, 2013 say about registering a share transfer deed?

Pardiwala explains: “Under Section 56(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, it is stated that:

- “A company shall not register a transfer of securities of the company, or the interest of a member in the company in the case of a company having no share capital, other than the transfer between persons both of whose names are entered as holders of beneficial interest in the records of a depository, unless a proper instrument of transfer, in such form as may be prescribed, duly stamped, dated and executed by or on behalf of the transferor and the transferee and specifying the name, address and occupation, if any, of the transferee has been delivered to the company by the transferor or the transferee within a period of sixty days from the date of execution, along with the certificate relating to the securities, or if no such certificate is in existence, along with the letter of allotment of securities.”

( Originally published on Jul 19, 2025 )

**Notes:** All timings are represented in 12-hour notation in local time of **Orem, United States** with DST adjustment (if applicable).

Hours which are past midnight are suffixed with next day date. In Panchang day starts and ends with sunrise.

**Panchang** is like time in **Vedic Astrology**. In Modern age people use Calendar and Clock to keep time but followers of Hinduism use Panchang for time keeping. Panchang tells not only Sunrise, Sunset, Moonrise and Moonset but also auspicious and inauspicious times in a day.

In other words, Panchang is a **Vedic clock**, which is valid only for the geo location for which it has been built. Hence, Panchang is created for each city in the world separately.

The number of core elements in Panchang are five, namely **Tithi**, **Nakshatra**, **Yoga**, **Karana** and **Var** i.e. weekday. With the help of these five elements and combining them with additional elements e.g. **Lagna**, Sunrise, Sunset, Moonrise, duration of day and night, zodiac positions of Chandra and Surya, multiple auspicious and inauspicious Yogas are formed.

Some Yoga which doesn't occur daily but randomly on any day are also included in Panchang. Drik Panchang includes [Bhadra](https://www.drikpanchang.com/panchang/bhadra-dates-timings.html), [Panchaka](https://www.drikpanchang.com/panchang/panchak-dates-timings.html), [Ganda Mula](https://www.drikpanchang.com/panchang/gandamool-dates-timings.html), [Vinchhudo](https://www.drikpanchang.com/gujarati/panchang/muhurat/vinchudo-date-time.html), [Dwipushkar Yoga](https://www.drikpanchang.com/yoga/dwipushkar-yoga-date-time.html), [Tripushkar Yoga](https://www.drikpanchang.com/yoga/tripushkar-yoga-date-time.html), [Ravi Pushya Yoga](https://www.drikpanchang.com/yoga/ravipushya-yoga-date-time.html), [Guru Pushya Yoga](https://www.drikpanchang.com/yoga/gurupushya-yoga-date-time.html), [Sarvartha Siddhi Yoga](https://www.drikpanchang.com/yoga/sarvarthasiddhi-yoga-date-time.html), [Amrit Siddhi Yoga](https://www.drikpanchang.com/yoga/amritsiddhi-yoga-date-time.html), [Ravi Yoga](https://www.drikpanchang.com/yoga/ravi-yoga-date-time.html), [Jwalamukhi Yoga](https://www.drikpanchang.com/panchang/yoga/jwalamukhi/jwalamukhi-yoga.html), **Aadal Yoga** and **Vidaal Yoga**, which is collection of important auspicious and inauspicious Yoga in Dainika Panchang which occurs randomly on any day.

Panchang is like Vedic clock which should be referred throughout the day. Some rituals which require daily reckoning of Panchang are -

01. **Brahma Muhurta** \- to wake up and to perform the first Puja in this Muhurta. All human begins are advised to get up during this auspicious Muhurta to begin religious activities as well as academic activities.
02. **Pratah Sandhya** \- a must ritual for followers of Hinduism and one of the three Sandhya when daily Puja is performed.
03. **Madhyahna Sandhya** \- daily Puja which is performed during the mid-day, and it overlaps with auspicious Abhijit Muhurta.
04. **Sayahna Sandhya** \- a must ritual for followers of Hinduism and one of the three Sandhya when daily Puja is performed.
05. **Rahu Kala** \- an inauspicious time when no auspicious work should be started. Rahu Kala is more prevalent in Southern states of India.
06. [**Abhijit Muhurta**](https://www.drikpanchang.com/muhurat/daily/abhijit-muhurat.html) \- an auspicious currency during the middle of the day, when any auspicious work can be performed when no auspicious Muhurta is available.
07. **Vijay Muhurta** \- time which is good to begin any journey to get success and achieve the purpose of the journey.
08. **Sankalpa** \- an integral part of Puja ritual, when determination is fortified by locking the moment in the space-time. Sankalpa required all five Panchang elements, including positions of Graha primarily [Chandra](https://www.drikpanchang.com/hindu-gods/navagraha/chandra/lord-chandra.html), [Surya](https://www.drikpanchang.com/hindu-gods/navagraha/surya/lord-surya.html) and [Brihaspati](https://www.drikpanchang.com/hindu-gods/navagraha/guru/lord-guru.html).
09. **Sunrise** \- Performing [Surya Namaskar](https://www.drikpanchang.com/vedic-mantra/gods/navagraha/lord-surya/mantra/surya-namaskara-mantra.html) and **giving Arghya to rising Surya** requires exact time of Sunrise. Panchang is required on daily basis as Sunrise time keeps changing throughout the year.
10. **Moonrise** \- Many rituals are linked to Chandra Dev. Worshipping rising Chandra is very significant ritual during [Sankashti Chaturthi](https://www.drikpanchang.com/vrats/sankashti-chaturthi-dates.html) and [Krishna Janmashtami](https://www.drikpanchang.com/dashavatara/lord-krishna/krishna-janmashtami-date-time.html).

Above examples are just drop in the ocean and there are numerous ways, Panchang is used by the followers of Hinduism. Upcoming festivals and fasting days, various significant auspicious and inauspicious Yogas are also reckoned with Dainika Panchang.

title: ED raids Gurugram, Delhi in $15 million illegal call centre scam; assets worth Rs 100 cr unearthed
text:
New Delhi, Aug 23 
 The Directorate of Enforcement (ED) has unearthed a massive cyber fraud linked to illegal call centres operating from the National Capital, exposing a network that duped US citizens of nearly $15 million (approx. Rs 130 crore). 
 The agency carried out search operations on August 20, 2025, at seven locations in Gurugram and New Delhi under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA), 2002. The probe is based on a case registered by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI), Delhi, which alleged that a syndicate of cyber fraudsters conspired to cheat foreign nationals through fake tech-support call centres between November 2022 and April 2024. 
 According to ED, three accused -- Arjun Gulati, Divyansh Goel, and Abhinav Kalra -- were running call centres in Noida and Gurugram, posing as technical support providers to unsuspecting US citizens. Once trust was established, they gained unauthorised access to victims’ bank accounts, siphoning off funds that were routed through multiple foreign and Indian accounts. 
 Investigators revealed that the money trail spanned more than 200 bank accounts, layering transactions to mask the illicit proceeds. 
 The fraudulently obtained funds were eventually repatriated to India and invested in luxury lifestyles. The raids led to the seizure of incriminating documents, digital records, and recorded statements of key individuals that detailed the modus operandi of the racket. 
 Officials also froze 30 bank accounts directly linked to the accused. In addition, ED seized eight high-end luxury cars, several expensive watches, and properties allegedly acquired through the scam. 
 The total value of assets traced so far exceeds Rs 100 crore. 
 “The accused persons are living in luxury big houses, allegedly purchased through illegally earned money through cyber scam, and also acquired numerous valuable assets of more than Rs. 100 Crore from the Proceeds of Crime," the agency said in its press statement. 
 The crackdown highlights the growing trend of international cyber fraud being routed through India-based call centres targeting foreign nationals. ED officials confirmed that the case remains under active investigation.
